name: quilm
author: everyday-object semantics (lateral)
description: Seven-segment growth pairs. Clue: 'N K' with K in 3..6 digits and K+2 <= N <= 4K. Solution: two K-digit strings 'X Y' (space separated). Read each digit as a seven-segment display glyph (masks 0..9 = 63,6,91,79,102,109,125,7,127,111). For every position, the segments of X's digit must be a STRICT subset of the segments of Y's digit (i.e. Y's digit is X's digit with one or more extra segments switched on: 1->7, 5->6, 3->9, 0->8, 7->0, 1->8, ...), and the TOTAL number of segments added over all K positions must equal N exactly. Per-digit gains available: 1 {0>8,3>9,5>6,5>9,9>8}, 2 {1>4,2>8,3>8,4>9,5>8,6>8,7>3}, 3 {1>3,4>8,7>0,7>9}, 4 {1>0,1>9,7>8}, 5 {1>8}. Intended discovery path: demos show two same-length numbers where the right one is always 'fatter' (8/9 common on the right, 1 and 2 impossible there, 8 impossible on the left); the player has to ask what makes 1->7, 5->6, 3->9 and 0->8 the same move, land on the digital display, and then read the clue's first number as a count of added segments and the second as the digit count. Degenerate witnesses closed: empty and the clue itself (wrong shape); single-symbol answers (K>=3); X==Y and padding a short answer with unchanged digits (growth must be strict at every position); and the 'all 1s -> all 7s' family, which needs only one fact about the display, because N >= K+2 forces at least one position to gain 2 or more. solve() never emits a canonical witness: it picks a random composition of N and a random realising pair per position. PRIVATE: never shown to players.
